<reason>A won because it kept a cleaner decision rule—after notice, basic exclusion is either priced or permitted—and forced B to name a non-fine cost that actually makes repair cheaper for an ordinary public form. B’s best live argument was the platform-exit incentive, but it never showed why that risk defeats scaled, notice-based fines rather than supporting calibration. B also slipped by recasting existing lawsuits and agencies as already doing the work A had already called a lottery, while alternatives either lacked a price or recreated the shutdown B claimed to fear.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s Q1/A1 sequence: B never identified a non-fine cost that prices delay on a still-broken public form, and A used that to collapse scorecards, lawsuits, and “lose the channel” orders.</best_rebuttal>
